cards.intuition: Split the answer into atomic claims and check each one against the context. One invented number in a fluent paragraph is the exact failure this catches.
cards.topic: Faithfulness: Is the Answer Grounded in the Context

cards.intuition: An answer can faithfully repeat wrong context or be unfaithful yet correct from memory. Grounding and correctness are different defects with different owners.
cards.formula: faithful = supported by context, not = true
cards.topic: Faithfulness: Is the Answer Grounded in the Context

cards.intuition: Numbers, dates, and named entities are where hallucination hurts most and where verification is easiest, so decompose them with special care.
cards.topic: Faithfulness: Is the Answer Grounded in the Context

cards.intuition: It no longer matters that the evidence is somewhere in the index; it must be inside the chunks the generator actually sees.
cards.formula: needed evidence in sent chunks / all needed evidence

cards.intuition: Count how many sent chunks are useful and where they sit: models use the beginning and end of long contexts far better than the middle.
An irrelevant chunk is not neutral: it dilutes attention and can be woven into a confident wrong answer. Cut k or rerank harder.
A system can retrieve well and ground perfectly and still answer the wrong question. Relevance measures the answer against the ask.
cards.formula: does the response address the actual question

cards.intuition: When offline scores rise but escalations rise too, believe the escalations. Offline metrics exist to predict outcomes, not to override them.
cards.formula: thumbs, escalations, re-query rate are final

cards.intuition: Context metrics belong to retrieval, faithfulness to the grounding layer, relevance to generation and UX. One aggregate score destroys triage.
cards.formula: measure per axis, alert per axis

cards.intuition: LLM judges need calibration against human labels, pinned versions, and periodic re-validation, exactly like any measuring instrument.
cards.formula: validate on human labels, pin judge version
cards.topic: Evaluation Tooling: RAGAS, DeepEval, TruLens, and the LLM-Judge Pitfall

cards.intuition: Judges favor their own model family, reward length and confidence, and pass wrong answers that quote the right phrases. Design rubrics against all three.
cards.topic: Evaluation Tooling: RAGAS, DeepEval, TruLens, and the LLM-Judge Pitfall

cards.intuition: A human-labeled golden set gates releases, LLM-judged production sampling watches for drift, and online signals settle disagreements.
cards.formula: golden set -> CI gate, sampling -> drift, online -> arbiter
cards.topic: Evaluation Tooling: RAGAS, DeepEval, TruLens, and the LLM-Judge Pitfall
